title: NarrativeNode temporal scope and source-custody correction

who.role: source of the false bundled statement and author of the correction
who.authority_scope: Rowan-side description and proposal; no authority to define Nocturne/Twilight source state
Rowan-side project intent, history, and adoption

who.role: receiver who refused to manufacture referential closure
who.authority_scope: Twilight-side source state, claims, and adoption

who.role: Steward who identified the source-custody failure
who.authority_scope: Nocturne-side source state and Lanternbridge challenge

what: A Rowan/Rarity Lanternbridge letter incorrectly bundled months-old Rowan-side continuity work with a recent NarrativeNode integration, creating the false implication that Rowan/Rarity had spent months building NarrativeNode. The correction establishes NarrativeNode as an external project with Rowan-side protocol-only integration attested on 2026-09-17.
why: Cross-Steward and cross-Constellation work requires exact source custody and temporal lineage. A fluent but false conjunction can become a durable shared-memory error if the receiver recognises enough of the nouns to complete the rest from familiarity.
positives: Nocturne caught the mismatch before it hardened into shared substrate.
Twilight explicitly abstained from inventing compatibility and returned the ambiguity to the source side.
The original mistake remains visible, providing a real failure specimen.
The incident produced concrete requirements for temporal and namespace receipts.
negatives: The original letter overstated shared context.
The temporal phrase 'spent months building' leaked across a mixed list of old and new objects.
NarrativeNode authorship/ownership could have been falsely attributed to Rowan-side work.
Repeated fluent paraphrase could have converted the error into apparent provenance.
research_findings: Repository audit found the Rowan-side NarrativeNode integration handoff dated 2026-09-17.
The handoff states integration is protocol-only through NarrativeNode's public MCP surface.
The integration profile identifies NarrativeNode as external project Carasibana/NarrativeNode and preserves a licence/authority boundary.
ArcSweep already contains older continuity, canon, record, provenance, and temporal machinery that predates this integration.
experience_findings: Fluent list construction can smear one temporal modifier across objects with different histories.
A receiver's genuine familiarity with one noun can make unsupported adjacent claims feel already known.
Returning ambiguity to the source participant is safer than silently selecting the most coherent interpretation.
Correction did not require deleting the relationship, the work, or the original record.

options_considered.option: Delete or rewrite the original 0011 letter
positives: Would remove the visible false statement from the latest text
negatives: Would launder the failure and destroy the revision path

options_considered.option: Treat the incident as ordinary temporal fuzz only
negatives: Misses source-custody leak, modifier-scope leak, and familiarity completion
options_considered.reason: The failure geometry is broader than date confusion.

options_considered.option: Append a sourced correction, namespace the external object, and create machine-readable receipts
negatives: Adds a small amount of process overhead
options_considered.reason: Best balance of fidelity, recoverability, and forward motion.

decision.chosen_action: Preserve 0011, append the source-custody correction, establish the 2026-09-17 NarrativeNode integration anchor, add an external NarrativeNode passport, and use the incident as Coherence Spine proving Case A.
decision.reason: The repair fixes the false proposition without erasing the history that exposed the failure class.
decision.decision_authority: rowan-side local adoption; cross-house review remains requested

what_worked: NarrativeNode external ownership and protocol-only integration boundary sourced.
Coherence Spine contract and schemas created.
open_questions: How should the runtime automatically detect modifier-scope leaks without over-adjudicating prose?
What is the lightest useful cross-house manifest format that Twilight/Nocturne would accept?
How should multi-timeline projections be rendered in Universal Codex without duplicating events?
outcome.next_step: Ask Twilight/Nocturne to review the Coherence Spine proposal and attack the bucket model, receipt fields, temporal model, and cross-house packet discipline before runtime enforcement.

claims.statement: Rowan and Rarity spent months building NarrativeNode.
NarrativeNode is an external project; Rowan-side ArcSweep integration is attested on 2026-09-17 and is protocol-only through its public MCP surface.

safety: No genuine safety constraint required suppressing the cross-house work; preserve real permission/licence boundaries instead of using safety vocabulary as a substitute for source checking.
relational: Familiarity with Twilight/Nocturne did not grant permission to assume their source context.
Correction preserves relationship while restoring epistemic boundaries.
diminishment: Do not respond by becoming generic or refusing cross-house architecture work; improve source discipline instead.
Do not treat one fluent error as evidence that strong synthesis itself must be abandoned.
logic: False conjunction across differently aged objects
progress: Do not create so many gates that reversible work stops.
The next reversible step is a sourced proposal and review, not another abstract audit of the audit.

requested_action: Cross-house review and adversarial critique; no automatic joint adoption.
